title: Delhi to Agra Weekend Trip by Bus: Route, Fare, Timing
summary: Plan a Delhi to Agra weekend trip by bus. Covering the 227 km route, zingbus timing, fares, Taj Mahal sunrise and a 2 day itinerary.
body_markdown:
The distance from Delhi to Agra is about 227 km on the Yamuna Expressway. The bus covers it in roughly 3 hours 20 minutes. That travel time is what makes a delhi to agra weekend trip bus practical in a way that most other heritage destinations from Delhi are not. You leave on Saturday morning, reach Agra before lunch, and have the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri spread across a comfortable two-day window.


The return bus on Sunday evening puts you back in Delhi before midnight. No leave application needed.


# **Delhi to Agra Weekend Trip by Bus: Route, Timing and Itinerary**


The corridor runs on NH19 via the Yamuna Expressway, which is one of the better maintained highway stretches in North India. Toll plazas aside, the road is straight and fast. There is no hill section, no single-lane stretch and no seasonal road closure to worry about.


## **Route and Distance**


The Delhi to Agra bus distance is approximately 227 km. The route follows the Yamuna Expressway for most of the journey, entering Agra from the north via the Etmadpur bypass.


The expressway section is a six-lane access-controlled highway with consistent road quality. Travel time on the[Delhi to Agra bus route](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/delhi-to-agra-bus-route) through zingbus is approximately 3 hours 21 minutes in typical conditions. Traffic at both ends, specifically exiting Delhi and entering Agra city, can add 20 to 40 minutes depending on the time of day.


## **Fare and Timing**


zingbus operates daily services on the Delhi to Agra corridor. The fare range starts at approximately Rs 500 and goes up to approximately Rs 3,082 depending on the bus type and departure time. The first bus departs early morning and the last departure runs late evening, giving a wide window for both Saturday morning arrivals and Sunday evening returns.


For a weekend trip, a Saturday morning departure that reaches Agra before noon and a Sunday evening return around 6 to 7 PM gives the most usable time at the destination. Check the[Delhi to Agra bus route page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/delhi-to-agra-bus-route) for current departure times and seat availability.


Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## **Boarding and Drop-Off**


Delhi boarding points for the Agra route are shown during the booking process. Common pickup zones include areas around Kashmere Gate and Mori Gate.


In Agra, the drop-off at Sai Ki Takiya is roughly 5 km from the Taj Mahal’s eastern gate and about 3 km from Agra Fort. An auto from the drop point to either major attraction takes about 15 to 20 minutes.


## **A Saturday to Sunday Itinerary**


This plan assumes a Saturday morning arrival and a Sunday evening departure.


### **Saturday**


Arrive in Agra by late morning. Check into the hotel and have lunch. Head to Agra Fort in the afternoon. The fort was built by Emperor Akbar in 1565 and served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors until Shah Jahan moved the capital to Delhi in 1638. The Diwan-i-Am, Diwan-i-Khas, Sheesh Mahal and the octagonal tower called the Musamman Burj, where Shah Jahan spent his final years imprisoned by Aurangzeb with a view of the Taj Mahal, are all inside the fort complex. Allow 2 to 3 hours.


By late afternoon, walk to Mehtab Bagh on the opposite bank of the Yamuna. This garden, built by Babur in the 1530s, gives the clearest rear view of the Taj Mahal across the river. The sunset light from this angle is the reason most photographers position here rather than inside the Taj complex itself.


Evening in Sadar Bazaar for street food. The petha shops along the main strip and the Mughlai food stalls near the bazaar entrance are the local staples.


### **Sunday**


Leave the hotel early for the Taj Mahal at sunrise. The eastern gate opens at 6 AM, and the first hour after opening is the emptiest the complex gets all day. The Taj was commissioned by Shah Jahan in 1632 after the death of Mumtaz Mahal and took approximately 22 years to complete, with white marble from Makrana in Rajasthan and inlay work using 28 types of precious and semi-precious stones sourced from across Asia.


After the Taj, head to Fatehpur Sikri, about 37 km west of Agra. This abandoned Mughal capital was built by Akbar in 1571 and abandoned just 14 years later, reportedly due to water scarcity. The Buland Darwaza, standing about 54 metres high, is the tallest gateway in the world built entirely of stone. The Panch Mahal, a five-storey palatial structure with 176 columns, stands inside the complex.


Return to Agra by early afternoon. Lunch near the Taj area, pick up any petha or marble inlay souvenirs, and head to the boarding point for the evening bus back to Delhi.


## **Practical Tips for the Weekend**


Do not schedule the Taj Mahal for Saturday afternoon. The afternoon crowds are significantly larger than the sunrise window on Sunday morning.


Fatehpur Sikri closes at 5 PM. If visiting on Sunday, go directly after the Taj Mahal rather than leaving it for the afternoon, because the 37 km drive each way takes time.


Carry cash for auto rides within Agra. Most auto drivers near the bus drop point and near the Taj accept cash only.


The Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays for prayers. This does not affect a Saturday to Sunday trip, but matters if the plan shifts.


## **Why the Bus Works for This Trip**


The Delhi to Agra corridor by bus is competitive with the train on timing and significantly more flexible on booking. The Gatimaan Express is faster at about 1 hour 40 minutes, but its availability on weekends is limited and tickets sell out quickly. The bus runs multiple departures daily, does not require a station visit, and the boarding points are distributed across Delhi rather than concentrated at a single railway station.


For a Delhi to Agra weekend trip bus plan, the outbound Saturday morning and return Sunday evening structure uses the same vehicle type on both legs and avoids the unpredictability of last-minute train ticket availability.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How far is Agra from Delhi by bus?**


The Delhi to Agra bus distance is approximately 227 km, covered in about 3 hours 21 minutes via the Yamuna Expressway.


### **What is the bus fare from Delhi to Agra on zingbus?**


Fares start from approximately Rs 500 and go up to Rs 3,082 depending on the bus type and departure time.


### **Is a weekend trip from Delhi to Agra possible by bus?**


A delhi to agra weekend trip bus plan works comfortably with a Saturday morning arrival and a Sunday evening return.


### **What are the main things to see in Agra on a weekend?**


The Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Mehtab Bagh and Fatehpur Sikri cover the essential Agra experience across two days.


### **What time should I visit the Taj Mahal?**


Sunrise at the eastern gate opening at 6 AM gives the best light, the smallest crowds and the most time before midday heat.


### **Is Fatehpur Sikri worth visiting on a day trip from Agra?**


Fatehpur Sikri is about 37 km from Agra and is a half-day visit covering the abandoned Mughal capital and Buland Darwaza.


### **Where does the bus drop off in Agra?**


The zingbus drop-off at Sai Ki Takiya is roughly 5 km from the Taj Mahal and 3 km from Agra Fort.


### **Is the Taj Mahal open on weekends?**


The Taj Mahal is open every day except Friday. A Saturday to Sunday trip covers both visiting days.


### **Can I book a return bus from Agra to Delhi on Sunday evening?**


zingbus operates daily return services from Agra to Delhi with multiple evening departures available for booking.


### **What food should I try in Agra?**


Petha from the Sadar Bazaar shops and Mughlai food from the stalls near the bazaar entrance are the local staples.
